openingMessage: It takes time to create excellence. If it could be done quickly, more people would do it.
openingWhy: Nobody catches trapped pressure on a 'dead' line in his first month. That catch comes from a thousand honest LMRAs where nothing was wrong. Every real check you run today is buying the instinct that saves you in year five.
leadershipThought: Think before you speak. Think before you joke. Think before you act. Ask yourself: if this shows up in front of a client, my family, or leadership — does it represent me well? If the answer is no — don't do it.

specialFocus.title: Day Two: Watch Each Other's Backs, Starting With Your Partner
specialFocus.why:
Jacob, day two. Yesterday started with Mike's message. Today, make it practical: what watching each other's backs looks like on location and on the road. Thanksgiving is nine days out, and day two of a holiday week is still a full workday.

“Stay diligent, keep your head on a swivel, and watch each other's backs.”
— Mike Lyons
✓ SAY THESE NAMES
  • Bryan Medlin and Joseph Popillion, Shull Crawford 15OO 115H (Mon): gas showed when the bleed-off valves opened, and the casing was leaking. They called a hold point, made a plan and notified the right people. Popillion wrote it plainly: the crew wasn't comfortable doing the disconnect, so they used stop work. That's two partners watching each other's backs.
  • Andrew Bailey (Mon): three trailer inspections and the readiness form on 602, plus two air jobs. Nothing to fix.
  • Justin Fontenot (Mon): two air jobs, both close-outs complete. Nothing to fix.
  • Justin Pack, Hughes #1: nothing to fix Friday through Monday. Four days running. Marcos Morales, St Elmo: complete H2S daily Sunday and Monday, every answer Yes, every photo from the day.
  • Also clean Monday: Hayden Haugh, Trevor McKenzie, Humberto Marquez-Salazar, and on the ETX side Josh Blassingame and Brey Rasco.
  • Bobby Fleming and Kyle Williams (Sun): filed Commuting Journey Management Plans for the drive. That's the holiday-road habit we want from everybody this month.
👥 WATCH EACH OTHER'S BACKS: four checks
  • Look at your partner, not just the monitor. Before the first break: mask fit, monitor on, upwind. Ask "you good?" and wait for the answer.
  • If your partner stops the job, you stopped the job. Tick utilized on both forms. Monday, a crew used stop work over a leaking casing. It's written in the narrative, but no form ticked utilized.
  • Short gear is everybody's problem. If your trailer or your partner is short an SCBA, FRs or mask bags, say it before it rolls, and write down who you told.
  • Know your partner's drive home. Long drive? File the journey plan, and text when you're home.
Ten minutes: Mike's line (1) · names (2) · four checks (3) · the quiet partner (3) · send-off (1).
specialFocus.standardLabel: Week 23: Operational Discipline, and Your Partner Is Part of the Job
standard: The pre-task briefing takes two voices. If only one person talked, it wasn't a briefing.
LMRA out loud before the first wrench: what's changed since yesterday, and since the last well.
Verify controls with your own eyes, not the permit's, then have your partner check yours.
The routine job is the dangerous one. Your hundredth reconnect gets the same attention as your first.
Pressure is not authorization. "Let's get out of here," from anyone, including your partner, means slow down.
Drive like your family is in the truck. Phone down, journey plan on the long drives, and nobody drives tired.

scenarios.title: The Quiet Partner
scenarios.body: Your partner has been quiet all morning, and their phone keeps buzzing. Something's going on at home. At the second well they skip the mask check and start toward the wellhead. They're experienced, and it feels like none of your business. It is your business. "Hold up. You good?" Thirty seconds. Do the mask check together, then go. Jacob, ask the circle: on your worst day, what would you want your partner to say to you?

questions: Who is your partner today, and what's one thing you'll check for them before the first break?
If your partner stops the job today, what goes on your form?
What's your plan to get home safe for Thanksgiving, and who knows your route?
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: If your partner stops it, you stopped it: tick "utilized" on both forms. Phone down, eyes up, and nobody drives tired. We all go home for the holidays.
